articles.title: Sixers' Joel Embiid speaks on his health, how training camp is going
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Joel Embiid speaks on his health and how training camp has gone for himself and the team.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The Philadelphia 76ers will put their championship hopes on the play of their stars. The Sixers have one of the more talented rosters in the league, led by newcomers LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, but they're also counting on Joel Embiid to return to form.

Embiid has been battling a variety of injuries over the previous three seasons as he has not reached 40 games played in any of those seasons. When healthy, the big fella is still a dominant force as evidenced by his production, but health is always the operative word when it comes to the 2023 MVP winner. That is the biggest question with this group.

However, after a full summer to be work out and not have to worry about rehabbing from any injury, Embiid looks ready to roll. Especially, after a big block on teammate VJ Edgecombe in the Blue X White scrimmage on Saturday, which he claims he got all ball after being called for the foul.

"I thought I was all-ball," Embiid said with a sly smile only he can give.

Embiid then followed up that dunk with a lefty slam as he looked the best he has been at this early part of the season than he has in years.

"Pretty good," Embiid said of his health. "Not bad. I don't know, that's probably (he took a pause), I said I would never dunk again. In the moment, he did block me the first time so I was kind of pissed off about it. So I was hoping that he would jump again, so that's why I went for it. But, yeah, that's probably the last dunk of my career (he smiled)."

As far as how camp has gone during the week, Embiid has noticed a high intensity with this group. He and everybody else knows what is at stake in the upcoming season. This is an important year when considering the talent that they have accrued for this roster. Embiid, James, Brown, and others will be looking to lead Philadelphia to the franchise's first title since 1983.

"It's been good," said Embiid. "Obviously, new guys, but I've played with and against them for most of my career, so I know how to play. I think it's been, quite honestly, it's been easy. Everybody getting together, just playing. Yeah. It's always good to do this, but practice has been a little bit more intense and more fun. But it's been good so far."

As far as ways to accommodate his new star teammates, coach Nick Nurse hinted at a new offensive role for Embiid. The Sixers have been looking at different spots on the floor to utilize his vast skill set as he, James, and Brown do like to operate out of the mid-post. In an effort to get everybody in a rhythm on offense, it makes sense, but Embiid is ready to everything he needs for the Sixers to succeed.

"I mean, I can do everything on a basketball court, whether I'm at the top of the key, middle, left side, right side, 3-point line. So nothing changes," Embiid stated. "It's just about making sure everybody succeeds at the same time, and that's how we're going to have our success and how we're going to win."

The Sixers will begin the preseason on Monday when they play host to the New York Knicks.

articles.title: Bucs elevate QB Easton Stick from practice squad
articles.summary: The Buccaneers elevated linebacker Caden Fordham and quarterback Easton Stick from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Packers, the team announc...
articles.body:
The Buccaneers elevated linebacker Caden Fordham and quarterback Easton Stick from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Packers, the team announced.

This is the first elevation for both Fordham and Stick.

Stick will serve as the backup to rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, who is set to make his NFL starting debut in place of Baker Mayfield.

Mayfield will miss at least three weeks with a dislocated right thumb.

Stick signed with the Buccaneers' practice squad on Aug. 31.

Fordham signed with the Buccaneers as a rookie free agent in May and initially made the team's 53-player roster. The Bucs, though, waived him Sept. 2 after claiming cornerback Kevin Knowles off waivers from Kansas City. Fordham then signed back to the practice squad.

articles.title: Is Portadown's season finally up and running?
articles.summary: BBC Sport NI explores if Portadown's win over Limavady United will help kick-start their season.
articles.body:
Few would have expected David Jeffrey's return to management to be quite as difficult but, after eight weeks, Portadown have won their first game of the season.

Going into the latest weekend of Irish Premiership action, the Ports were the only team yet to register a win and sat four points adrift at the foot of the table.

However, a convincing 3-1 victory over Limavady United ended their winless run and offered Jeffrey and his players a much-needed lift.

But will this signal a turning point for the Ports? BBC Sport NI takes a look.

It was a tough opening few weeks for Irish League veteran David Jeffrey at the helm of his new club.

The 60-year-old has built his managerial reputation on producing teams that are organised, competitive and relentless, whether chasing titles at Linfield or guiding Ballymena United to League Cup success.

Yet during the opening weeks of this season, Portadown looked a long way off resembling a typical Jeffrey side.

However, that began to change against Limavady when glimpses of his style began to shine through with the side pushing forward in numbers and showing intensity.

Portadown had scored just five goals in their opening nine games but netted three times against a newly promoted Limavady side, who had won three of their past four games.

It will not just be the crucial three points that will please Jeffrey, but also the manner in which his side responded to setbacks throughout the game.

It was a nightmare start for the home side when Rhys Breen was forced off after just three minutes, but substitute James Teelan made an immediate impact and opened the scoring.

Having waited so long for their first win, Portadown could have easily let Limavady's quick equaliser unsettle them.

However, they responded in emphatic fashion and scored two goals during a clinical second-half display, with Limavady the side who struggled and the Ports unlucky to have not scored more.

'It is a new experience for me' - Jeffrey

For Jeffrey the result represented a welcome change of circumstances for a manager who is more accustomed to managing teams with ambitions of winning trophies, rather than a side struggling at the basement of the table.

After a two-year spell out of management, the 60-year-old said that his new challenge is unfamiliar territory.

"We find ourselves in a very difficult and disappointing place, there is no shying away from that," Jeffrey told BBC Sport NI.

"After a very positive pre-season, the season has been difficult and I felt, at times, we did not have the good fortune that our hard work deserved.

"The league table does not tell lies, and we just had to stick together as a group, staff and players.

"It is a new experience for me, but it was back to simple basics, self-belief and sticking by your players and staff. Making sure we work as hard as we can and hoping we get our reward on some occasion."

For Portadown, the challenge now is turning one positive result into something more sustainable, and Ben Kennedy could have an important part to play.

Every team, no matter if they are pushing for the Gibson Cup or trying to avoid a relegation battle, needs players who are capable of turning chances into goals.

Kennedy is no stranger to the Irish League and has already proven already during his career that he can influence games at this level.

The 29-year-old scored 39 goals and registered 23 assists during his 109 appearances for Crusaders before netting 16 goals at Ballymena United.

Last season did not go the way that Kennedy would have hoped and now, rediscovering form and full fitness is not only important for his new club, but also himself.

Working under former boss Jeffrey, someone he knows well, could help the striker re-establish himself as a consistent scorer in the Premiership.

Everyone knows that no two years in the Irish Premiership are the same and it remains too early to start discussing relegation battles.

However, last season provided a stark reminder of how damaging a poor start can be when Glenavon, who did not register a point from their opening 11 games, dropped to the Championship for the first time in 21 seasons despite an impressive second half of the season.

Portadown no longer have the unwanted distinction of being the only team in the division without a win and that should ease some of the pressure on the club.

But Jeffrey is far too experienced to get carried away by one result with a tough run of fixtures ahead for the side.

"No one is getting carried away," he continued.

"We did fantastically well against Linfield in a game which we could and should have won and then the next game Bangor taught us a lesson.

"You do not let your feet off the ground, it is nice to get a win, but our feet will be firmly nailed to the ground."

One victory will not erase the problems that Portadown faced in the opening weeks of the season, but it can change the mood around the club.

Their next match against in-form Glentoran will be key to see if the side simply enjoyed a welcome afternoon of relief or whether Jeffrey's outfit have finally found the beginning of something they can build on.
authors: Jana McCabe - BBC Sport NI journalist

articles.title: Super League Grand Final: Wakefield Trinity boss Daryl Powell on 'phenomenal, immense' run to title at Old Trafford
articles.summary: Wakefield Trinity comprehensively beat Warrington Wolves in Super League Grand Final on Saturday to clinch first league title for 58 years, becoming sixth team to win Super League; Wakefield were relegated in 2023, playing the 2024 season in the Championship under head coach Daryl Powell
articles.body:
Wakefield were crowned Super League champions for the first time in the club's history with a resounding 23-10 victory over Warrington Wolves in the Grand Final at Old Trafford, a week on from travelling to huge favourites Wigan Warriors and dispatching of them 33-6 in the semi-finals.

The success proved Wakefield's first league title for 58 years dating back to 1968, and all the more remarkable considering they were relegated from Super League in 2023, playing the 2024 season in the Championship under Powell.

"I'm just amazed really at the players and how good they've been," Powell said.

"Obviously it's pretty sweet for me as an individual but for the club, the players, the coaching staff, everything that we've built up over the last three years is phenomenal.

"We've been building for a while but the last two weeks in particular have been just incredible performances from an unbelievable group of players.

"The boys have got such confidence in each other, that if we all do our jobs then we can do anything we want. We've done that this year. It's just immense.

"It's been an amazing finish to the season, wow. I couldn't speak more highly of the boys about everything they do, really.

"I know there's quite a few boys in there who just can't believe it. That we've been able to do all that.

"But it's just a testament to how good they are. I'm so proud of everything. The club, the fans - the way that they've been - obviously the players. They are just such a pleasure to coach and be around. It makes it an easy job."

For Powell, 61, it was his first time leading a side out in a Super League Grand Final since 2017, when he was Castleford Tigers head coach and lost heavily to Leeds Rhinos.

Saturday's success was made even sweeter for Powell by the fact it came against Warrington, where he coached for two seasons before being dismissed in 2023.

"This is the best [achievement], really," he added. "It looked like maybe I'd slip through my career and not win the big game after 2017 and it's been a long time.

"I had a tough time at Warrington, and then to come back and do this with Wakefield, it's phenomenal.

"For me, it's right up there. Just being at Wakefield and feeling at home again in a place and being able to get a group of men together who can do special things, it's unbelievable.

"I've had some great times in my coaching career, but this is the best."

'I felt this year might be one too early - but this club can go anywhere'

Backed by an outspoken and ambitious owner in Matt Ellis, Powell admits clinching the Super League title this year was even beyond his own wild expectations and hopes.

He now believes his team and the club can kick on even more.

"This club can do anything, really," he says.

"I felt like this year might be one year too early for us but the boys have proven me wrong.

"I felt like next year, maybe. I'm so pleased for the players, you can't write that stuff, can you? It's unbelievable.

"You don't know when you're going to have another chance at this sort of stuff. I feel there's a lot of love in this team and group.

"It's kind of a bit soppy at times, but wow, what a group of men. I'm so proud to be associated with them.

"It shows special things can be achieved.

"Some other clubs have done great things, maybe at different timescales, but this is an unbelievable story. From me thinking a bloke was trying to sell me a kitchen [owner Matt Ellis] to winning the Super League trophy. It's been an unbelievable three years."

Jowitt: A rollercoaster of a year for me - highs are worth the lows

"A million per cent the highs are worth the lows.

"It didn't feel real that we were playing a Grand Final until we got here today.

"A rollercoaster of a year for me personally after dropping down to the reserves, not finding form, but I got my opportunity at the back end of the year.

"For this to be my last game for Wakefield, I will never forget it."

'Emotional' Johnstone: I can't believe it - my dream for the last decade!

Rob Burrow Award winner Tom Johnstone to Sky Sports:

"I can't quite believe it. I keep crying, I can't help myself! Such a special club, it's been the longest week of my life.

"To get out there and get it done, I don't know what to say.

"This club means eveyrthing to me. I've been saying it for a long time. My dream the last 10 years was to win a Grand Final with Wakefield.

"Daryl Powell sold me the dream that we were a club that had aspirations and wanted to win things.

"I believed every word they said and this is where we are now.

"We don't do this without that belief we have. We built our foundation on that."

articles.title: World Grand Prix: Luke Humphries beats James Wade to secure final showdown with Gerwyn Price
articles.summary: World number two Luke Humphries clinched his spot in the final of the World Grand Prix with a 5-3 victory over James Wade where he will face Gerwyn Price after his 5-2 win over Nathan Aspinall.
articles.body:
World number two Luke Humphries secured his place in the World Grand Prix final with a 5-3 victory over James Wade.

Humphries averaged 96.92 and threw 10 180s as he reached the final for the fourth successive time.

The 31-year-old Englishman will face Welshman Gerwyn Price on Sunday evening in Leicester after he beat Nathan Aspinall in the other semi-final.

"I've got to do it again because there's so many major finals I've let slip. Gezzy [Price] is playing well but if I play like that again, it's going to be a cracking game and I hope it is," Humphries told Sky Sports.

"To make four Grand Prix finals on the trot is super special. It's history for myself and I'm proud of that but unless I pick that trophy up, unfortunately that history doesn't mean anything."

Humphries, who won this title in 2023 but has lost in the past two finals, took the opening set of the semi-final but Wade produced a brilliant 141 checkout en route to drawing level.

The pair exchanged the next two sets before Humphries took control of the contest to move 4-2 ahead.

Wade refused to go quietly and pulled one back to keep the match alive but Humphries held his nerve in the eighth set to seal victory on double top.

In the other semi-final, Price beat a spirited Aspinall 5-2.

The Welshman took a three-set lead as Aspinall struggled to reproduce the form that had seen him average 105.15 in his quarter-final win over Ryan Joyce.

Aspinall briefly rallied and produced a superb 132 checkout - the highest of the match - to get a set on the board.

The 35-year-old then threatened to turn the match around when he reduced the deficit to one set at 3-2.

However, Price regained his composure and closed out the next two sets without reply to secure his place in the final.

Price said he was "frustrated" by Aspinall's antics during the match as he interacted with a partisan crowd at the Mattioli Arena.

"I'm glad to come through the game. Nathan was complaining about the crowd, but they were on his side," Price said.

"He's performing a little bit on stage. I'm great friends with Nathan, but take it on the chin sometimes when you're losing."

articles.title: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries to face Gerywn Price in Sunday's final in Leicester, live on Sky Sports
articles.summary: Luke Humphries reaches fourth straight World Grand Prix final after beating two-time champion James Wade in semis; Gerwyn Price defeats Nathan Aspinall as he targets first major title since 2022; watch live on Sky Sports+ and Sky Sports Main Event from 8pm Sunday
articles.body:
Price, the 2020 champion, beat Nathan Aspinall 5-2 in Saturday's first semi-final before 2023 winner Luke Humphries defeated James Wade 5-3 to reach his fourth straight final and set up a repeat of the showpiece game three years ago - when he saw off Price 5-2.

A major drought will end either way at the Mattioli Arena, with Humphries going over a year since his last premier title - the 2025 Premier League - and Price's previous elite silverware coming way back in 2022 at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

The final, in which the winner will earn £150,000 and runner-up £80,000, will be first to six sets, with Humphries hoping to fare better than he did in 2024 and 2025, when he lost 6-4 to Mike De Decker and 6-1 to Luke Littler respectively.​​​

Price prevails after being frustrated by Aspinall antics

Price romped into a 3-0 lead over Aspinall, peeling off two 13-darters and then a 15-darter to sweep the opener before he broke The Asp in the deciding leg of set two.

The third set went on throw until the fourth leg, when Aspinall missed six darts to hold, including two at double one, and Price subsequently pinned D10 to move 3-0 up.

Things seemed bleak for Aspinall when Price broke in 14 darts at the start of the fourth set, only for The Asp to win back-to-back legs with well-thrown darts at D16 around failed ones before pulling back a set with a stunning 132 finish featuring two bullseyes.

The 2022 runner-up won the fifth set against the throw but Price did likewise in the sixth to move one away from victory and then broke Aspinall twice in a row in the seventh set, after being broken himself, to qualify for a fourth Grand Prix final following 2020, 2021 and 2023.

Speaking afterwards, Price said he had been annoyed by Aspinall complaining about the rowdy crowd, telling Sky Sports : "I was upset with him a little bit. I said, 'they're on your side bud, I'm up against it'.

"As good as the crowd is for me, they were all for him. He's performing a little bit on stage. I'm good friends with Nathan, but sometimes you've got to let your darts go. It did [affect my game]."

'Controlled' Humphries into another Leicester final

Later, Humphries ended Wade's hopes of a third World Grand Prix crown, and first since 2010.

'Cool Hand' won the sixth set on throw after the first five had been taken 3-1 by the player throwing second.

Wade, who produced the checkout of the game with a 141 in the second set but largely struggled to hit the mandatory leg-opening double, took the next stanza, but Humphries was not to be denied, firing in back-to-back 137s to break 'The Machine' in the eighth set around two holds of throw.

Humphries, who had beaten Dave Chisnall, Jermaine Wattimena and Niels Zonneveld prior to knocking out Wade, told Sky Sports: "I did say I was going to play a lot better and I did - I felt a lot more relaxed.

"That was the real me there today and I'm really proud of myself for performing like that. It's been a long time since I've felt that control and not like I was going to flounder a little bit.

"To make four Grand Prix finals on the trot is super special. It's history and I'm proud of that but unless I pick that trophy up, unfortunately that history doesn't mean anything.

"I've got to do it again [on Sunday] because there's so many major finals I've let slip. Gezzy [Price] is playing well but if I play like that again, it's going to be a cracking game."

articles.title: Florida Gators run into buzzsaw in Missouri, Tigers shred top-ten team for rare ranked win at home
articles.summary: Austin Simmons threw for 340 yards and two scores as the Missouri Tigers demolished the No. 8 Florida Gators 45-17, holding Jadan Baugh to 13 yards.
articles.body: The Florida Gators certainly aren't the 2019 LSU Tigers. They might not even be the 2019 version of the Florida Gators. The number eight team in the country traveled to Columbia, Missouri, and ran into an absolute buzzsaw, as the Tigers took the Gators behind the woodshed in a 45-17 victory on Saturday. FLORIDA GATORS FACE MISSOURI TIGERS IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL MATCHUP WHERE THE OVER LOOKS LIKE THE PLAY It seemed like anything that could go right for Mizzou did. The Tigers were able to establish their dominance on both lines of scrimmage, putting up 560 total yards and holding Florida to a shockingly low 42 yards on the ground. Jadan Baugh, who came into the game leading the SEC in rushing yards, could hardly get it going this afternoon, only rushing for 13 yards on 12 carries. The former Ole Miss starter was about as perfect as anyone could have asked for, eviscerating Florida's secondary to the tune of 340 yards and two scores through the air. Missouri showed a ton of resolve, regrouping from their loss last week to Mississippi State and winning a home game against a ranked opponent for the first time since 2024. For the Gators, Faurot Field has proved to be a house of horrors, and Saturday afternoon was no different. The game was never close after halftime, and at no point did the usually explosive Florida offense look threatening to the home team. Now, first year head coach Jon Sumrall will have to regroup and answer some tough questions. It doesn't get any easier for the Gators either. articles.title: FSU football report card for Virginia game
articles.summary: The FSU Seminoles beat the Virginia Cavaliers, but what grades do the players and coaches deserve?
articles.body:
The FSU Seminoles have their biggest win of the season, crushing the Virginia Cavaliers 38-7 in Doak Campbell Stadium.

FSU scored the final 38 points of the game to erase a first-quarter deficit and cruise to victory. It was a massive win for the Seminoles, who improved to 3-2 overall and 1-1 in ACC play with the win. While his seat is still hot, this helped cool it off and gives them some momentum ahead of a tough stretch of ACC games.

While quarterback Ashton Daniels led the way with a record-setting performance, he was far from the only Seminole to have a great game. The defense finally showed its talents, wracking up 10.0 sacks and 12.5 tackles for loss, to the delight of their fans .

Here is our report card for FSU's Week 5 win over Virginia.

Daniels had the game of his life, writing his name into FSU's record books. His five rushing touchdowns are the most ever by a Seminole, and should unlock something the offense can build on moving forward. He finished with 136 yards on the ground to go with 183 yards and one interception passing.

Ousmane Kromah and Quintrevion Wisner took a backseat to Daniels in the game, but they made the most of their chances, combining for 126 yards on 26 carries. Wisner also took a screen pass for 48 yards, setting up FSU's first touchdown. Kromah once again forced several missed tackles, needing to be gang-tackled by Virginia.

FSU had 183 yards receiving, but it came on just 12 receptions as they frequently generated explosive plays, setting up the rushing attack. Micahi Danzy had his best game of the season, catching a team-high four passes for 70 yards. The group also did a good job blocking, helping squeeze some extra yards out on run plays.

They had a rough start to the game, but FSU's offensive line settled in as the game went on and did a good job of protecting Daniels in the second half after giving up 3.0 sacks in the first quarter, some of which were partially on Daniels. Xavier Chaplin was called for two penalties, an area he has to improve in.

FSU's defensive line dominated the game, frequently getting pressure on Beau Pribulla and containing Virginia's run game. Rylan Kennedy had his best game as a Seminole, recording a team-high 2.0 sacks. Kevin Wynn had the first sack of his career, and six different defensive linemen had a sack.

Chris Jones has been exactly what FSU needed at linebacker, and he had another great game. He and Mikai Gbayor led the team with six tackles apiece, with Jones having 1.5 sacks and two quarterback hurries while Gbayor added one sack of his own. The group, along with the defensive line, did an excellent job stopping Virginia's rushing attack and preventing Pribulla from scrambling.

They were helped out by some drops, but the secondary did a good job sticking with their guys and avoided any costly busts, something that has plagued them this season. Pribulla completed 14 of his 32 passes for 168 yards and one touchdown.

Gabe Panikowski continued his perfect start to the season, making his only field goal and all five extra points. Daniel Hughes averaged 47.2 yards on his five punts, with two going for over 50 yards and one being pinned inside the 20-yard line. His only blemish was a 33-yarder that gave Virginia a short field before they scored their touchdown.

Jasen Lopez once again looked dangerous returning punts, returning four for 43 yards. He had a 31-yarder that helped set up FSU's second touchdown. FSU's coverage team also did a good job, allowing just one punt return for 13 yards.

It took a quarter, but FSU completely dominated this game. The decision to let Daniels pound the rock was an excellent one and is how he should be used moving forward. The defense looked completely different than they have all season, a testament to Tony White and the rest of the coaching staff.

articles.title: Hawkeye Football: Instant Reaction Iowa Overmatched by Ohio State 31-14
articles.summary: The Hawkeyes pass defense bends and breaks as Jeremiah Smith and Julian Sayin take to the air.
articles.body:
The Hawks put themselves in an early hole, with Brown fumbling on their first series and OSU recovering at their 14-yard line. In the blink of an eye Ohio State was up 7 – 0 and it never felt good from there on out. Iowa did pass on multiple first downs and attempted 32 pass attempts to 21 rushes. And the Hawks did end the day with 199 yards passing, but it was nowhere near enough to consistently move the ball down the field and score points. Not to mention keep OSU's offense off the field by competing in the possession game with a reliable rushing attack.

The final score and way that OSU got there was close to what many predicted. However, Iowa ended the day with a mere 39 total yards rushing against an OSU rush defense that appeared to be more vulnerable than recent years pass. And Brown was regularly hurried, sacked multiple times, and as mentioned started off Iowa's first series with a fumble as he was being sacked deep in Iowa's own territory.

Iowa started this season with a stable of running backs and an offensive line that looked like it picked up from where it left off last season. Now we are left wondering if the Hawks can establish a running game against a solid defensive opponent.

Some of our worst fears were realized as OSU's lethal passing one-two punch came to fruition. One of college football's most accurate passers, Julian Sayin, was 20/27 for 74% for 324 yards. Jeremiah Smith had 206 of those yards by himself as his record setting season continued. The best news about Smith is that since he's now broken most every record he can and is a third-year player it's likely this will be the last time Iowa has to face him.

The other good news is that Iowa just faced two stout defenses and finished the opening act 1 – 1, and we can only hope some of the worst is over as they prepare to head west to Washington.

Zach Lutmer left the game injured in the third quarter and was taken to the locker room. Deshaun Lee also was injured in the third quarter and was on the sideline later in the game without his helmet. During his post-game comments Kirk Fertentz did say that some of the players that came out during the game were cramping up, so time will tell while Iowa has a short week to get ready for their next opponent.

Special teams was once again a consistent performer for Iowa for the most part. Boston Everitt had 2 punts downed inside the 20 with at least one downed at the three-yard line. Caden Buhr was 2/2 on his field goal attempts with a long of 48. The special team's only self-inflicted wound was the second half kickoff that went out of bounds and let OSU start at the 35.

Jeremy Hecklinski did enter the game in the fourth quarter and provided some energy and a positive drive that included 5/5 passing for 67 yards and a touchdown topped with a two-point conversion to bring Iowa to a respectable (not embarrassing?) 14 points on the day. It was good to see Heck get additional game experience to keep him ready when called upon.

To end with a grounded, forward-looking perspective, at the start of this season we all knew that Iowa's first three Big Ten games to open the season would be a gauntlet. Many felt that if Iowa could escape those three games 1 – 2 and open the first six games at 4 – 2 it was a realistic expectation, and perhaps as good as could be hoped for. Now Iowa turns towards Washington, a team that currently does not appear to be as daunting as originally expected. Iowa will start their front end loaded schedule at no worse than 4-2 with the possibility of getting to 5 – 1 heading into their bye week.

articles.title: Ah Yat throws 5 TD passes, Davis has 205 yards receiving as Montana beats Northern Colorado 36-14
articles.summary: (AP) — Keali’i Ah Yat threw five touchdown passes, Brooks Davis caught three scores and finished with a career-best 205 yards receiving, and Montana beat Nor...
articles.body:
MISSOULA, Mont. (AP) — Keali'i Ah Yat threw five touchdown passes, Brooks Davis caught three scores and finished with a career-best 205 yards receiving, and Montana beat Northern Colorado 36-14 on Saturday.

articles.title: Tyson Bagent is expected to start for the Bears on Sunday vs. Jets
articles.summary: Case Keenum will take a seat on the bench, after beating the Eagles on Monday night.
articles.body:
The Bears are deferring to their depth chart.

Despite Monday night's win by third-string quarterback Case Keenum over the Eagles, the Bears will apparently turn to second-stringer Tyson Bagent on Sunday against the Jets.

Via Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Bagent is expected to start the game .

Although the Bears have tried to keep the identity of the starter a secret , the signs have pointed to Bagent . He took the first-team reps during practice on Wednesday and Thursday — and possibly Friday.

Coach Ben Johnson hasn't announced a starter for the Week 4 game. Does he need to? Bagent is listed as the backup to starter Caleb Williams. Bagent didn't play on Monday night, given that he was able to practice all week while in the concussion protocol.

Keenum got the Week 3 start against the Eagles. With Bagent cleared, the Bears have decided not to ignore the preordained configuration of quarterbacks, even though Keenum managed to engineer a 27-7 win over the Eagles.

Undrafted out of Shepherd, Bagent started four games in 2023, his rookie year. He has made eight appearances since then. Most recently, he replaced Williams in the fourth quarter of the Week 2 loss to the Vikings. Bagent nearly pulled off the victory.

articles.title: What Josh Heupel said about Faizon Brandon, benching for Tennessee football
articles.summary: Josh Heupel said he pulled quarterback Faizon Brandon in the second quarter of Tennessee football's win over Auburn on Oct. 3. at Neyland Stadium.
articles.body:
Tennessee football coach Josh Heupel turned to sophomore quarterback George MacIntyre in relief of freshman Faizon Brandon midway through a 24-14 win for the Vols against Auburn at Neyland Stadium on Oct. 3.

Brandon was in the middle of the worst game of his still young career, having completed only three of eight passes for zero yards and an interception before being pulled with 3:42 left in the second quarter. Heupel said postgame the Vols (4-1, 1-1 SEC) will continue to evaluate the quarterback competition moving forward.

"Faizon, ultimately, didn't play his best football," Heupel said. "But I've said it a bunch ... we're going to need them all throughout the course of the year. ... The guys that had to step up did and we'll be back in the building on Monday and continue to grow. There's a lot of growth left for us on the offensive side of the football."

Tennessee football, Faizon Brandon vs Auburn, see our best photos | Exclusive

Heupel told the ESPN broadcast at halftime that Brandon "just wasn't operating" and that he "wasn't feeling 100%." But postgame, he downplayed the impact of any discomfort Brandon felt lingering from the loss to No. 1 Texas on Sept. 26.

"I don't know that I would say that," Heupel said postgame when asked if Brandon's health affected his performance. "We'll watch a little bit of the tape and see more of it. But we'll go from there."

Brandon wasn't listed on any of the injury reports in the week leading up to the Auburn game despite taking 10 sacks and a number of other vicious hits against Texas.

He exited the Texas game in the second quarter after suffering an apparent injury, but only missed a handful of plays before returning to the game. Brandon completed 17 of 29 passes for 145 yards, a touchdown and no interceptions in the 20-17 defeat at Neyland Stadium.

In relief of Brandon, MacIntyre threw for 86 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions while completing 80% of his passes. The Vols were able to protect him, too. Auburn (3-2, 1-2) sacked Brandon twice in less than two full quarters but got to MacIntyre only once.

MacIntyre was able to lean on 220 rushing yards and three touchdowns from running back DeSean Bishop.

articles.title: IceHogs kick off season with annual block party in downtown Rockford
articles.summary: Fans gathered in downtown Rockford on Saturday for the IceHogs' annual block party to celebrate the start of the new season before their opening-night game a...
articles.body:
ROCKFORD, Ill. (WTVO) — Fans packed downtown Rockford on Saturday for the Rockford IceHogs' annual block party to kick off a new season.

The annual event featured free craft beer tasting, free coffee, kids' activities, a T-shirt giveaway, local food trucks, and live music by That 70's band, along with a live radio broadcast. But the biggest draw was the players themselves, as fans lined up along the red carpet to meet the team as they entered the BMO Center ahead of their opening-night matchup against the Milwaukee Admirals.

Derrick Carter attended the event. He said he was excited to be part of the festivities and looked forward to what he hopes will be a successful season for the IceHogs.

"The whole celebration for the Screw City opening night is going to be bonkers," Carter said, referring to the IceHogs' Screw City alternate uniforms and the team's whiteout promotion. "The whole fanbase is going to be wild."

Scott Carnes, a season-ticket holder for the past decade, shared Carter's excitement and said the Rockford community should continue supporting its hometown team.

"It's good for the community," Carnes said. "Rockford needs to show their support for the team, so it's nice to see the lines of people coming out."

As the regular season begins, fans said events like the block party help build excitement and bring the community together in support of the hometown team.

articles.title: Kentucky takes out South Carolina in OT: 3 things to know and postgame cheers
articles.summary: The Comeback Cats secured a massive OT win after falling behind by 17 points.
articles.body:
In an absolutely thrilling fashion, the Kentucky Wildcats beat the South Carolina Gamecocks in overtime on Saturday afternoon in Columbia by a final score of 35-34.

The Cats got off to an abysmal start that seemingly put the game out of reach before it even really started. The Gamecocks took control early, driving the ball down the field at will. Kentucky couldn't get anything going on either side of the ball as Shane Beamer's squad took a commanding 17-0 lead. However, Kentucky clawed its way back to a 20-10 deficit before halftime.

After the break, a battle ensued. Kentucky showed pure resiliency as they fought and scraped to take the lead from the Gamecocks. However, LaNorris Sellers and Co. answered when they needed to. The Cats played an incredible third quarter, yet again, before taking a 24-20 lead that they surrendered right back to South Carolina.

A field goal late in the fourth quarter tied it at 27-27, and it'd stay that way into overtime.

In OT, South Carolina scored first, and Kentucky answered right back. But they didn't settle for the extra point. Will Stein decided to go for two, and he GOT IT! This was the largest come-from-behind road win in program history. What a win!!

Next up, the Cats will return home for one of their biggest tests yet as they'll take on the LSU Tigers next Saturday night.

Kentucky stays behind the sticks too often

There has been a lot of talk about Kentucky's woes on third down this season, but it's much more than that. They haven't been good on third downs, but it's because they don't put themselves in a good position to succeed.

Kentucky gives up a lot of sacks and tackles for loss, which can completely blow up a drive. If the running game isn't working, like it wasn't today, it forces the Cats to put a lot into Kenny Minchey's hands, and that's just not his game. No offense is good when playing behind the sticks. The protection was poor early on, and the negative results followed.

Will Stein and Joe Sloan have got to figure out a way to get UK into better positioning on first and second down, so that they have a real chance to convert when third down comes. Situational football is really important, but it's not just third and fourth downs (which Kentucky had success with in this game).

As creative as these coaches are, I have to think they'll figure it out. This offense is waiting to break out, and a few adjustments could make all the difference. Look no further than how that second half and overtime went.

Imagine how good this team can be when it puts four good quarters together.

Kenny Minchey is a really good game manager

I mean this in a complimentary way. Minchey is really good at managing the offense, sometimes even masterful, and when needed, he can make winning plays.

He doesn't make many mistakes, but he misses some big throws. He keeps the offense churning and protects the football, but he rarely lets it loose to a receiver running down the sideline, and he is really hesitant to tuck the ball and run.

LaNorris Sellers carried the Gamecock offense and gave them chance after chance. Minchey answered when Kentucky needed it most, including his two game-winning throws at the end of OT.

Stein and Sloan make Minchey's job much easier as they simply ask him to play within himself and execute their scheming guys open, and Minchey is getting it done.

Occasionally, Minchey makes the play himself, but usually, he's just executing the X's and O's. Now, that might seem like a shot rather than a compliment, but let me be clear: Not every quarterback can run this offense. Finding the right guy is more important than finding the more talented or most athletic guy.

I think Minchey is a perfect fit. That's my quarterback.

Man, I'm really not sure that I need to say anything else, but I will anyway because I can't get enough of this kid. Darby was the first big-time recruit that Stein was able to secure (thanks, Joe Sloan), and it is sure paying dividends.

Darby is a true freshman wide receiver who stands at just 6'1 and 180 pounds. Most were excited about his potential, but I don't think anyone expected what he's provided this season just due to his size alone. Don't let it fool you. I think DJ Miller is UK's best receiver, but Darby leads the team in receiving yards, and that lead got a lot bigger after this game.

With Miller out and the offense stalling, Darby stepped up time and again. Nothing can get this kid down. As you remember, he dropped a touchdown pass against Texas A&M, but he responded with a touchdown and multiple catches after.

In this game, he made an unbelievable diving catch, but it was somehow overturned in an inexplicable ruling. It didn't faze the kid at all. He just kept on doing what we've come to expect—making play after play after play.

Darby is a big play threat, but he's more than just that. He takes crossing routes over the middle. He can take a screen to the house. You never know what you're going to get with Darby, but it's almost always going to be fun.

Ohio State football fans watched with excitement in Week 5 as Jeremiah Smith became the team's all-time leader in receptions, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. "I wanna congratulate you bro on breaking every record, man," Parris Campbell, a former OSU receiver, said.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Congratulations on the triple crown, it's been special watching you put your name in the record books," Hill added in a video viewed over 8,000 times as of Saturday afternoon.

The Buckeyes began the day with news of coach Ryan Day's classy message to Iowa's Stead Family Children's Hospital . Day's team outgained Iowa 484 yards to 238, one week after Iowa's thrilling upset victory over the Michigan Wolverines in Ann Arbor. Smith made the extraordinary look like par for the course yet again, racking up 11 catches for 206 yards and two touchdowns in the Buckeyes' Big Ten road win.

October 10 brings a golden opportunity for the Buckeyes to hone their skills against the Maryland Terrapins on the road before a colossal matchup with Curt Cignetti's defending Big Ten Champion Indiana Hoosiers on October 17 in Bloomington.

The college football landscape has changed dramatically in recent years, but Ohio State just keeps on winning. Smith looks Heisman-worthy and Bucks look playoff worthy, but college football is chock full of parity putting the onus on Day's team to stay sharp ahead of more challenging games yet to come.

BOULDER, Colo. (AP) — Deion Sanders made a switch at quarterback Saturday night in an effort to spark a stagnant Colorado offense, inserting Isaac Wilson over highly touted prospect Julian "JuJu" Lewis.

The Buffaloes coach hinted at a switch leading into their game against No. 12 Texas Tech. Wilson, a transfer from Utah, entered the contest a week ago when Lewis struggled. Lewis, who recently turned 19, started the first four games of the season after showing promise a season ago.

Wilson quickly settled in Saturday and led the Buffaloes on a nine-play, 75-yard drive that culminated with the QB throwing an 8-yard touchdown to Joseph Williams. Wilson's first snap as the starter wasn't a throw but a catch. He hauled in a 7-yard pass from Kaneal Sweetwyne on a trick play.

Wilson also had a carry for 7 yards on the drive. Wilson is the younger brother of Zach Wilson, the former standout at BYU who's now with the New Orleans Saints.

Lewis emerged as the QB of the future last season. He showed his talent in a win over Weber State on Sept. 12. He threw for 366 yards and four TDs — he ran for another — in earning Big 12 freshman of the week honors. He was replaced at halftime in a loss at Baylor last weekend.

articles.title: 3 takeaways: Malik Washington struggles as Maryland is routed by Nebraska, 48-23
articles.summary: Exhales. Here we go again. ‘Same old Maryland.’ Another Saturday, another demoralizing ending. The Terps fell to Nebraska, 48-23, on Saturday to stretch thei...
articles.body:
Another Saturday, another demoralizing ending. The Terps fell to Nebraska, 48-23, on Saturday to stretch their losing streak to three since opening FBS play against Virginia Tech on Sept. 19 in coach Michael Locksley's eighth year at the helm.

Maryland led for most of the first half, building a lead as large as nine points in the second quarter, but never fully took control against the Cornhuskers. The Terps allowed 34 unanswered points from the 2:41 mark of the second quarter to the end of the game. Quarterback Malik Washington delivered another uneven performance, following last week's stinker by recording only 77 more passing yards after throwing for 177 in the first quarter, including zero in the second quarter.

And in a theme that has become all too familiar during the Locksley era, Maryland repeatedly undermined itself with costly mistakes.

A week after throwing four interceptions against UCLA , Washington's turnover problems followed him to Nebraska.

Washington finished the game 23-for-44 for 254 yards and a touchdown, but a pair of first-half interceptions prevented the Terps from building on an early lead.

His first pick came with Maryland leading 16-14 after Nebraska scored a touchdown on the opening drive of the second quarter. On the Terps' first play of the ensuing possession, Washington dropped a pass directly into the hands of defensive lineman Kade Pietrzak, who had dropped into coverage.

Nebraska failed to capitalize, and Maryland scored a touchdown on its next drive after DeJuan Williams picked up 59 yards by himself on two plays. Washington's next interception, however, had much costlier implications.

With Maryland driving at the Nebraska 25-yard line, leading by nine with 2:41 remaining in the half, Washington lofted a pass that defensive back Dwayne McDougle III intercepted and returned 81 yards for a touchdown. The score cut Maryland's lead to two, and Nebraska grabbed the lead before halftime.

Add it up for Washington over the past two weeks: six interceptions, three returned for touchdowns.

It's not the sophomore leap Maryland expected.

Self-inflicted mistakes and more self-inflicted mistakes

It didn't take long for Maryland to show "the standard" of shooting itself in the foot. That's a joke, but it's the same stuff with this team.

After Bryce McPherson nearly had a punt blocked on Maryland's first possession — only to benefit from a roughing-the-kicker penalty that helped extend the drive and eventually produce a field goal — Nebraska got him the second time. Jeremiah Charles was credited with the block, and the Cornhuskers promptly turned it into points on a 19-yard touchdown run from Mekhi Nelson.

Here's another play that led directly to a score: Late in the first quarter, Anthony Colandrea was sacked by Carlton Smith for an 11-yard loss, setting up third-and-27. Instead, Nahsir Taylor came down on him after the play and ripped his helmet off in the process, drawing a penalty and giving Nebraska new life.

Naturally, the Cornhuskers went down and scored.

Those two plays alone turned what could have been a 16-0 Maryland lead into a 16-14 game.

Then came the penalties. Nebraska had its share, in fairness, but Maryland piled up 70 penalty yards in the first half, including an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty and a personal foul on freshman Zion Elee. The latter came during Nebraska's 80-yard touchdown drive to close the half.

On that final drive alone, Maryland was flagged for a personal foul, holding, roughing the passer and offsides.

The offensive execution wasn't much better. Maryland didn't convert its first third down until the fourth quarter and finished 1-for-14. Over the past two games, Maryland is 2-for-29 on third down.

There's also the fourth quarter. Nebraska led by only five entering the final period before outscoring Maryland, 20-0. Despite Locksley and Washington repeatedly emphasizing that winning the fourth quarter was a priority this season, the Terps have struggled to do so consistently.

Maryland has not won a fourth quarter in Big Ten play since Oct. 26, 2024, against Minnesota — 707 days ago.

Earlier this week, Maryland athletic director Jim Smith publicly backed Locksley, saying the two were "aligned on the work in front of us" after the Terps' 54-3 loss to UCLA.

Four days later, that work produced more of the same.

Smith said his statement this week would be his final public comment on Locksley's job status. That doesn't mean the questions are going away.

If anything, they're only getting louder.

Maryland travels to Ohio State next week before hosting a struggling Rutgers team Oct. 17 ahead of its bye week. Locksley would be owed roughly $10 million if fired before Jan. 1, 2027, an obvious factor in any decision.

But at some point, the results become impossible to separate from the coach.

After another loss filled with the same mistakes, that point might be getting closer.

articles.title: Louisville football's Jeff Brohm responds to player eligibility ruling
articles.summary: After UofL football's loss to NC State, coach Jeff Brohm talked about two players who recently were ruled ineligible by the Kentucky Court of Appeals.
articles.body:
Cornerback Jabari Mack got his first start of the season in Week 4 against Wake Forest and was listed as an "or" starter with Tayon Holloway on Louisville's depth chart.

But less than 24 hours before the Cardinals' Week 5 game at NC State, Mack and linebacker Kalib Perry were ruled ineligible after a panel of three judges from the Kentucky Court of Appeals threw out a temporary restraining order from the Jefferson County Circuit Court that previously allowed them to play.

"As far as the high school class of 2022 was concerned, there was no loss of an opportunity for them because nothing changed, and the new rule did not, as the circuit court surmised, 'bar' them from doing anything they previously had a right to do. Permitting the high school class of 2022 to play a fifth season — the very relief the respondents were requesting in their joint motion for a 'temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction' — would disrupt the status quo."

UofL head coach Jeff Brohm didn't use not having the two as an excuse for the Cardinals' 31-28 loss to NC State, however.

"Yes, you want to have key players out there," Brohm said. "But at the same time, the others can perform better, and we can be much better as a team no matter who's in there. And that's our job as coaches to make sure that we're doing that."

Mack had previously played in the first four games of the season, totaling seven tackles and three pass breakups. Perry, who had just become eligible Sept. 14, played in the past two games; he had one tackle in each.

Mack had first earned eligibility for a fifth season almost two months ago, when the 2022 recruiting class was included in the NCAA's new five-year eligibility rule. The organization was then granted a stay request, which denied Mack and those from the high school graduating Class of 2022 a fifth year.

The back-and-forth eligibility battle continued when Mack and, eventually, Perry were part of a lawsuit filed with the Jefferson County Circuit Court that led to the TRO that granted them eligibility. Things took another turn in the eligible-ineligible battle Oct. 2 when the group's lawsuit was dissolved.

"Jabari and Kalib Perry are big parts of our package, but it doesn't matter," Brohm added. "Who's in there has to play better. So, I don't know (if) that will ever resurface again. We're probably going to just have to continue to improve with the guys we have and make improvements, be way better and coach way better."

Courier Journal reporters Brooks Holton and Payton Titus contributed to this report.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts’ downfield passing offers hope for struggling Eagles
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts ranks third in yards per attempt on throws of at least 10 air yards, offering a bright spot amid Philadelphia’s offensive struggles
articles.body:
Philadelphia's offensive struggles have overshadowed an encouraging part of Jalen Hurts' early-season performance. When the Eagles quarterback attacks beyond the short passing game, he has produced at a rate that places him near the top of the NFL. Entering Week 4, Hurts is averaging 14.6 yards per attempt on throws traveling at least 10 air yards. Only Joe Burrow, at 14.8, and Josh Allen, at 14.7, rank ahead of him.

Downfield efficiency offers something to build around

The statistic does not erase Philadelphia's slow starts, turnovers, or inconsistent execution. It does show that the Eagles have generated meaningful production when Hurts pushes the ball farther downfield.

These are throws of at least 10 air yards, a category that includes intermediate attempts alongside deeper passes. That distinction matters when evaluating how Philadelphia can build on the success. The answer does not have to be a steady diet of low-percentage shots.

Better protection, cleaner timing, and favorable early-down situations could give Hurts more opportunities to attack those areas without forcing the offense into difficult decisions.

DeVonta Smith's absence creates another test

With Smith ruled out against the Rams , the Eagles must find ways to preserve that production through Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, and their complementary targets.

The challenge is turning an encouraging passing split into a more consistent offensive performance. Hurts has demonstrated that Philadelphia can gain substantial yardage beyond the short area. Maintaining that efficiency with a depleted receiving group would give the Eagles a stronger chance to rebound Sunday.

articles.title: Final Chiefs injury report ahead of Week 4 game vs. Raiders
articles.summary: Chiefs carry a remarkably healthy roster into an AFC West rivalry matchup, though one setback on the offensive front requires an adjustment The Kansas City C...
articles.body:
Chiefs carry a remarkably healthy roster into an AFC West rivalry matchup, though one setback on the offensive front requires an adjustment

The Kansas City Chiefs are preparing to defend home turf in a pivotal Week 4 clash against their longtime division rivals. Navigating the opening month of an NFL campaign regularly tests roster endurance, but Andy Reid's squad enters this rivalry weekend in premier physical shape.

While a dozen players surfaced on the preliminary practice sheets throughout the week, Friday's final designations brought overwhelmingly positive news. Kansas City will have virtually every frontline playmaker ready for action on Sunday afternoon.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The lone significant injury concern sits on the offensive line. Tackle Josh Simmons has officially been ruled out for Week 4 after failing to practice at all during the week. Simmons logged consecutive non-participation tags on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday while battling an ongoing back injury.

His absence tests Kansas City's perimeter blocking depth, forcing line coach Andy Heck to rely on his tackle rotation to keep the pocket clean and open rushing lanes on early downs.

Aside from Simmons, the Chiefs avoided handing a single questionable tag to any other player on the active roster.

Key offensive leaders show no limitations heading into Sunday

Patrick Mahomes was listed on the injury report with a knee issue, but his inclusion proved to be strictly procedural. The franchise quarterback took every first-team rep throughout the week, logging full participation on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. Mahomes carries no injury designation into the weekend and will lead the offense without restriction.

Wide receiver Rashee Rice was also monitored during the week due to a knee issue. Rice silenced any concerns about his availability by working as a full participant in every practice session. With his speed, route running and yards-after-catch ability intact, Rice remains primed to serve as a primary target over the middle and across the intermediate areas of the field.

Defensive stars and secondary pieces cleared for kickoff

Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo received a clean sweep of clearances across every level of his defense, ensuring his unit can attack with full personnel packages.

All-Pro defensive tackle Chris Jones managed a calf injury throughout the week but handled full workloads across Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. Jones brings his trademark interior disruption into Sunday without a game status tag. On the edge, defensive ends Felix Anudike-Uzomah and Ashton Gillotte both shook off physical ailments to log full participation all three days.

Anudike-Uzomah managed a quad issue, while Gillotte worked through a knee concern. Linebacker Jack Cochrane rounded out the front-seven clearances, practicing fully despite a calf issue.

The secondary saw equally encouraging progress. Cornerback L'Jarius Sneed opened the week with consecutive limited sessions on Wednesday and Thursday while managing a knee issue. However, Sneed ramped up his activity on Friday, logging a full practice that removed any doubt about his status for Sunday.

Defensive backs Chamarri Conner and Jadon Canady each handled full practices Wednesday through Friday while managing knee ailments. Cornerback Christian Roland-Wallace also avoided an injury designation after participating fully on Wednesday despite a shoulder concern, sitting out subsequent days purely for maintenance.

With every defensive back cleared to dress, Kansas City enters Sunday's divisional showcase with complete scheme versatility and depth across the entire roster.
